facts.text: After the parser processes an utterance, the result is handed on to the discourse history, one of SmartKom's most elaborate modules, which acts as the memory of the entire system, tracking who said what and what was presented.

facts.text: The discourse history helps with anaphora resolution and fills in structures that are omitted from an utterance, using information carried over from earlier in the discourse.

facts.text: Since not every module in SmartKom keeps a memory of everything that happened, the discourse model adds information into the system's representations at each dialogue step, unless the person is actually rejecting what happened before.

facts.text: The discourse model also helps coordinate gesture and screen issues, storing what was presented at what location on the screen when a person points to something.

facts.text: The discourse model has a clear interface that can be queried, for example to check whether admission fees were discussed in the last turn or in earlier turns, with control over how deep to search back.

relations.text: The discourse history module receives its input from the parser's intention-parsing output.
relations.source_quote: what happens is you know the parser parses it and then it 's handed on to the discourse history

relations.text: Because the discourse history stores the system's whole memory of what was said and presented, it is what makes anaphora resolution, gap-filling, and queryable lookups (such as whether admission fees were discussed earlier) possible.
